chapter: Billy Berg's, Granz and Nat Cole
title: The Four Brothers concerts at Normandie Hall
summary: Willard describes the weekly Saturday sessions promoted by Jimmy Talbert and others around 1951, and Callender's own dances with Talbert.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: We were talking about the sessions... Well, first you were talking about Norman Granz' beginnings as a promoter in Normandie Hall, which later the Four Brothers presented concerts there in the early Fifties, the Four Brothers not being Herman's Four Brothers, but James Talbert, Irving Ashby... Remember those sessions?
Oh yeah. You're talking about Normandie Hall again.
Normandie Hall again. It was about 1951, every Saturday night at Normandie Hall. You used to play on some of those.

Yes, I did. And speaking of Talbert, he and I did a few things on our own. One was at a place on Vernon and Central Avenue upstairs. There was a hall there. I can't think of the name of it. But we promoted a couple of dances there. It didn't make any money, but we promoted them...

Well, the ones at Normandie Hall didn't really make any money, I don't think. Because Jimmy used to come by... Jimmy, who is now attorney James Talbert, and who was also the nephew of Lee and Lester Young. But at that point he was like a law student and a Jazz fan. He played a little himself. But Jimmy, Irving Ashby, and a disk jockey from Alaska named Jerome...I can't remember Jerome's last name...and a writer named Joe Bernard. Those were the Four Brothers. And they were The Four Brothers Present at Normandie Hall. And some amazing music was played there every Saturday night for a year or so. But he used to come by and pick up my unemployment check to help put the deposit down with the union, I remember!
That's funny. Unemployment checks were about $18 a week.

Something like that. He would get my whole check on Thursday, and I could have it back if I went up to Normandie Hall on Saturday night -- and I always got it back. But he ended up just breaking even, I think, every Saturday night.
Well, he was lucky if he broke even.
